                                                                                                                                      The correct answer is concentric circles.

                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                      Key Points

                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor form concentric circles.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • The direction of these magnetic field lines can be determined using the Right-Hand Rule.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • As the distance from the conductor increases, the spacing between the concentric circles increases, indicating that the magnetic field strength decreases.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • The magnetic field lines are perpendicular to the current-carrying conductor.
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • This phenomenon is described by Ampere's Circuital Law, which relates the magnetic field around a conductor to the current passing through it.
                                                                                                                                        • \n
                                                                                                                                      \n\n

                                                                                                                                      Additional Information

                                                                                                                                      \n\n
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Magnetic Field\n\n\t
                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • Magnetic fields are produced by electric currents, which can be macroscopic currents in wires, or microscopic currents associated with electrons in atomic orbits.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Electromagnetism\n\t
                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • Electromagnetism is a branch of physics involving the study of the electromagnetic force, a type of physical interaction that occurs between electrically charged particles.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • It encompasses various phenomena such as electricity, magnetism, and light.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
                                                                                                                                        • \n\t
                                                                                                                                      • Faraday's Law of Induction\n\t
                                                                                                                                          \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • Faraday's Law states that a change in the magnetic field within a closed loop induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the wire.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t\t
                                                                                                                                        • This principle is the working mechanism behind electric generators and transformers.
                                                                                                                                          • \n\t
                                                                                                                                        \n\t
